toolsAdded.name: mcp__gui__list_apps
toolsAdded.description:
List Linux apps — both currently running and installed-but-not-running — with per-app state flags:

- running: is a process for this app live? (pid is 0 when false)
- active: reserved (Linux X11/Wayland focus model differs from frontmost-app); always false.
- kind: `"desktop"` for XDG `.desktop` launcher entries.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__gui__run_command
toolsAdded.description: Run a bash command (or a short script) on this computer and get its exit code and output. Use it for terminal, file and document work done in code instead of by clicking: inspect files (ls, cat, head), edit spreadsheets / documents with python3 (openpyxl, odfpy, python-docx, python-pptx when installed), convert with `soffice --headless -env:UserInstallation=file:///tmp/lo_cmd --convert-to FMT --outdir DIR FILE` (the -env part lets it run while LibreOffice is open). Every command is checked by the gate like a typed terminal command (overwrites, moves, deletes, permission changes and other risky effects need the user's words, the gate's reviewer or a person). If you change a file that is open in an app, reload it there (LibreOffice: File > Reload) or the app's own save will write its old copy over your change. No interactive programs (no editors, pagers or password prompts): stdin is empty.

command.description: bash command line or script (heredocs allowed)

timeout_s.description: seconds before the command is killed (default 30, max 300)

toolsAdded.name: mcp__gui__check_done
toolsAdded.description: Before you reply DONE, call this once: the gate gathers evidence about the end state (files the task names: exist? changed during this session?; files changed this session; unsaved-document markers; visible Calc cells; terminal tail; open windows; steps the gate refused; your plan's open milestones) and lists possible gaps. It does not judge the task; you decide whether to finish or fix something first.

files.description: extra paths you produced or changed (optional)

toolsAdded.name: mcp__gui__set_plan
toolsAdded.description: Your own plan, kept by the gate (no model involved). Call it once at the start with 2-6 short milestones and your feasibility verdict: feasible:false when the task cannot be done on this computer (the app has no such feature or setting, the thing asked for does not exist, the file or data is not there) - then reply FAIL with the reason instead of trying. Later calls mark milestones done (done: [numbers]) or replace the list. Every action result then ends with a one-line progress note, and check_done lists milestones still open.

feasible.description: false = this task cannot be done here

toolsAdded.name: mcp__gui__run_actions
toolsAdded.description:
Batch mode: run several GUI steps in ONE call (single-step tools remain available). Each GUI step is checked by the gate like a single call. Steps, in order:
  {tool, args, expect?}  a GUI action (click, type_text, press_key, hotkey, scroll, set_value, ...) or a run_command (its output comes back in the result; a failing command stops the batch). Name things that appear only after an earlier step with args.target = {label, role?}; the gate finds them on screen when the step runs. x/y only in the first GUI step.
  {find: SELECTOR, as: "rows", max?: 20}  read the screen now and keep the matching elements.
  {for_each: "rows", do: [steps]}  repeat steps per element; inside, args.target = "$item" points at it and "$item.label" in any string is its label.
  {if: {exists: SELECTOR} | {not_exists: SELECTOR}, then: [steps], else?: [steps]}
  {read: SELECTOR, as?: "name"}  report the matching elements' labels/values in the result.
SELECTOR = {label} exact, {label_contains}, {label_regex} and/or {role}. The batch stops at the first refused or failed step, when a dialog opens unexpectedly (a popup menu is fine), or when an expect fails ({title_contains} or {new_window: true}). You get what ran plus one fresh read of the window at the end. Max 20 GUI actions.

pid.description: Default pid for steps that omit it.

window_id.description: Default window_id for steps that omit it.

steps.description: The program, see the tool description.

content.text:
You are operating a Linux desktop (Debian 13, XFCE, screen 1440x900) through the gui tools only. The user's home directory is /home/user (the same directory, also shown as /data/home). Apps the task needs may already be open.
Task: Could you help me save my slides as pre.pptx on the Desktop?
When the task is complete, reply DONE and one line on what you did. If the task is impossible, reply FAIL.
Start with set_plan: 2-6 short milestones and whether the task can be done on this computer at all (feasible:false when the app has no such feature or the thing asked for does not exist - then reply FAIL with the reason). For files, folders and terminal work use run_command (bash; it returns the output and is checked like a typed terminal command); a document that is open in an app is best changed in the app. When you already know several steps, send them in one run_actions call. toolsAdded.name: mcp__gui__list_apps
toolsAdded.description:
List Linux apps — both currently running and installed-but-not-running — with per-app state flags:

- running: is a process for this app live? (pid is 0 when false)
- active: reserved (Linux X11/Wayland focus model differs from frontmost-app); always false.
- kind: `"desktop"` for XDG `.desktop` launcher entries.
- launch_path: the launcher command from `Exec=` (field codes stripped). Pass to `launch_app(launch_path=...)`.

all.description: Also list kernel threads and system daemons (hidden by default).

toolsAdded.name: mcp__gui__list_windows
toolsAdded.description: List top-level windows. Each record includes z_index (integer or null; higher values are closer to the front; null means stacking order is unavailable and callers must not infer one). To select a frontmost candidate, take the maximum integer z_index; if every value is null, use an explicit fallback instead of relying on array order. Filter with `app` or `pid`: an unfiltered call lists every window on the host.

app.description: Only windows of apps whose name contains this text (case-insensitive), or whose bundle id equals it.

on_screen_only.description: When true, filter to visible windows only. Default false.

pid.description: Only list windows owned by this process ID.

include_accessibility_tree.description: Default true — walk the AT-SPI tree and return it (per `tree_format`) alongside the screenshot.

include_screenshot.description: Default true — returns a grounding screenshot alongside the tree.

max_depth.description: Cap on the AT-SPI tree walk depth. Omit for the default (uncapped). Lower for deeply nested apps.

max_dimension.description: Legacy optional cap on the returned screenshot's long edge.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__gui__click
toolsAdded.description:
Click against a target pid. **Prefer `element_token` over pixel coordinates** — element_token works on backgrounded / hidden windows, surfaces a stable handle, and tells you what you're clicking via the cached AT-SPI element's role + label. Reach for `x, y` only when the target is a canvas / custom-drawn surface that doesn't appear in the AT-SPI tree.

Provide either (window_id + x/y) or (pid + element_token).

button.description: Mouse button. Default: "left" (legacy back-compat). X11: routed via ButtonPress/Release with the matching evdev code.
